mainTopic: What counts as an ornament versus a burden on שבת: קמיע and תפילין, rings for men and women, and the herb bundle (כובלת)
overview: The amud opens by asking whether a person wearing a קמיע might take it off and carry it on שבת. The גמרא says a leather-covered קמיע may stay on even in the בית הכסא. It explains that תפילין are different because of the exposed שי״ן, and אביי adds that the שי״ן, דל״ת and יו״ד of תפילין are all הלכה למשה מסיני. After defining the armor words of the earlier משנה, a new משנה lists five items a woman may not go out with, including a sealed ring and a כובלת. עולא says the ring rules are reversed for a man, and רב יוסף explains that for clothing, women are 'a people unto themselves.' אביי's challenge from found תפילין is answered with רבי מאיר's view that women are obligated in תפילין. רבא explains that wearing a ring on the finger while delivering it is a normal way of carrying. Finally, a ברייתא brings three views on the herb bundle, משאוי or תכשיט, and settles that רבי אליעזר permits it לכתחילה.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא warns against holding a קמיע and carrying it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that a person wearing a קמיע never takes it off. It cites רבי אושעיא, who warns him not to hold it in his hand and carry it four אמות ברשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא that רבי אושעיא says: as long as he does not hold it in his hand and carry it four cubits in the public domain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that a קמיע can stay on the body at all times, even in the בית הכסא. A ברייתא shows that people do take it off and hold it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier logic said there is no fear of carrying on שבת, because he never needs to remove the קמיע. רבי אושעיא's warning shows a real case where he takes it into his hand. That suggests the קמיע has קדושה and must be removed before entering the בית הכסא.

keyTerms.meaning: An amulet, often containing written holy words
As long as / provided that
Four cubits, the distance that counts as carrying
The public domain

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Oshaya says:
phrases.notes: Classic opening of a challenge from a ברייתא

phrases.english: As long as he does not hold it in his hand
and carry it four cubits in the public domain!
phrases.notes: Wearing is allowed, but carrying it in the hand is not

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the prior assumption, on the previous amud, that a קמיע is never removed and so poses no carrying risk.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a person can keep a קמיע on even in the בית הכסא, so he never takes it off.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אושעיא's warning shows a real case where the קמיע ends up in his hand. That implies it must sometimes be removed, presumably because of its קדושה.

steps.title: The case is an amulet covered in leather
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we are dealing with a קמיע covered in leather. Since the writing is covered, he may keep it on in the בית הכסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, with what are we dealing here? With an amulet covered in leather.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends itself by narrowing the case to a קמיע whose writing is wrapped in leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the holy writing is covered, bringing it into the בית הכסא is not a disgrace. So he never needs to remove it, and there is no fear he will carry it on שבת. רבי אושעיא's warning would then refer to an uncovered קמיע.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (narrows the case)
Covered / wrapped
Leather

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: The word in brackets shows up only in some versions.

phrases.english: With one covered in leather.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any קמיע with writing must be removed before the בית הכסא, so it ends up in his hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: A leather-covered קמיע may stay on in the בית הכסא, so there is no carrying risk.

steps.title: תפילין are covered in leather yet must be removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: תפילין are also covered in leather, yet a ברייתא says one must remove them four אמות before entering a בית הכסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But תפילין are covered in leather, and it was taught: one who enters a bathroom removes the תפילין at a distance of four cubits and then enters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 2 by pointing to תפילין, which also have leather-covered writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If leather covering solved the problem, תפילין should be allowed in the בית הכסא too. Yet the ברייתא requires removing them, and even at a distance of four אמות. So leather covering seems not to help.

keyTerms.meaning: But behold / but consider (introduces a counterexample)
Phylacteries
Bathroom / lavatory
Removes
At a distance of

steps.confusionAlert: The four אמות here are not about carrying on שבת like in step 1. They are the distance from the בית הכסא at which one takes off the תפילין.

phrases.english: But behold, phylacteries, which are covered in leather,
and it was taught: One who enters a bathroom

phrases.aramaic: חוֹלֵץ תְּפִילִּין בְּרִחוּק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְנִכְנָס.
phrases.english: removes the phylacteries at a distance of four cubits and enters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the leather-covering answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that leather covering lets holy writing enter the בית הכסא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין are leather-covered, yet they must be removed. So leather covering should not help a קמיע either.

steps.title: תפילין differ because of the exposed letter שי״ן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תפילין are different because of the letter שי״ן on the outside of the box. אביי says this שי״ן is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is because of the שי״ן, as אביי said: the שי״ן of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why תפילין must be removed even though the scrolls inside are covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with תפילין is not the covered parchment inside. It is the שי״ן on the outside of the leather, which is exposed holy lettering with Sinai authority. A leather-covered קמיע has no such exposed letter, so it may stay on.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other case)
Because of
The letter שי״ן formed on the outside of the head תפילין
A law given orally to משה at Sinai

steps.whatToRemember: A leather-covered קמיע may enter the בית הכסא. תפילין may not, because the שי״ן is exposed on the outside and is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the principle that covered holy writing is protected from disgrace, while exposed holy letters are not.

phrases.english: There, it is because of the shin.
As Abaye said: The shin of phylacteries
is a law given to Moses at Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by showing that תפילין are a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תפילין must be removed because of their covered parchment, which would mean covering does not help.
steps.terutzMaskana: תפילין must be removed because of the exposed שי״ן, so covered writing in a קמיע is still allowed.

steps.title: אביי adds the דל״ת and יו״ד of תפילין
steps.stepSummary: Having quoted אביי on the שי״ן, the גמרא adds two more of his statements. The דל״ת and the יו״ד of תפילין are also הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: the דל״ת of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני. And אביי said: the יו״ד of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two more related teachings from אביי, about the other letters formed on תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These statements are attached because they follow the same pattern as the שי״ן teaching. The דל״ת is the knot of the head strap, and the יו״ד is the knot by the arm תפילין. Together with the שי״ן they spell שַׁדַּי, a holy Name, all of Sinai authority.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter דל״ת, formed by the knot of the head strap
The letter יו״ד, formed by the knot at the arm תפילין
Divine Name spelled by שי״ן, דל״ת, יו״ד

steps.whatToRemember: The שי״ן, דל״ת, and יו״ד of תפילין are each a הלכה למשה מסיני, and together they spell שַׁדַּי.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: The dalet of phylacteries
is a law given to Moses at Sinai.
And Abaye said: The yod of phylacteries
is a law given to Moses at Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two related statements of אביי alongside the שי״ן teaching of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The דל״ת and יו״ד of תפילין, like the שי״ן, are each a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Defining the armor words in the earlier משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier משנה and explains three armor words: שריון, קסדא and מגפיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a man may not go out on שבת with a שריון, a קסדא, or מגפיים. A שריון is a coat of mail. A קסדא, says רב, is a leather cap. מגפיים, says רב, are leg armor.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about קמיע and תפילין is finished. The גמרא returns to the earlier משנה and explains three hard words for pieces of armor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words were unfamiliar, so the גמרא gives their meanings in everyday Aramaic. שריון is armor made of scales. קסדא is a leather cap worn under a metal helmet. מגפיים are armor worn on the legs below the knee. Once we know what each item is, we understand what a man may not wear out on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A coat of mail, explained by the גמרא as זַרְדָּא
A helmet item. רב explains it as סַנְוָארְתָא, a leather cap worn under a metal helmet
Leg armor. רב explains it as פֻּזְמָקֵי

phrases.english: And not with a shiryon
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the earlier משנה about what a man may not go out with.

phrases.english: nor with a kasda
nor with maggafayim.
Shiryon means a coat of mail.
phrases.notes: This is armor made of scales. No name is attached to this explanation.

phrases.english: Kasda: Rav said it is a leather cap.
phrases.notes: It is worn under a metal helmet.

phrases.english: Maggafayim: Rav said it is leg armor.
phrases.notes: It is worn below the knee.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא בְּשִׁרְיוֹן וְלֹא בְּקַסְדָּא וְלֹא בְּמַגָּפַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The קמיע and תפילין discussion (steps 1 to 5) is done. The גמרא now goes back to the next words of the earlier משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שריון is a coat of mail. קסדא is a leather cap (רב). מגפיים are leg armor (רב). A man may not go out with these on שבת.

steps.title: New משנה: five items a woman may not go out with
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists five items a woman may not wear or carry into רשות הרבים on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman may not go out on שבת with a needle that has a hole, with a ring that has a seal on it, with a כוליאר, with a כובלת, or with a flask of balsam oil.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists five things a woman may not go out with on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה listed items for a man. This one lists items for a woman. A sewing needle with an eye is a tool, not jewelry. A ring with a seal is used to stamp things. Wearing items like these outside can count as carrying in רשות הרבים. The גמרא will explain later what a כוליאר and a כובלת are.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה
A needle with a hole, meaning an ordinary sewing needle with an eye
A ring with a seal on it, used for stamping
A woman's item whose identity the גמרא discusses later
A small flask of balsam oil, used as perfume

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman may not go out
phrases.notes: This means going out to רשות הרבים on שבת.

phrases.english: with a perforated needle
phrases.notes: An ordinary needle with an eye for thread.

phrases.english: nor with a ring that has a seal on it
nor with a kulyar
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains this word later.

phrases.english: nor with a kovelet
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains this word later.

phrases.english: nor with a flask of balsam oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion of the earlier משנה is finished. A new משנה starts with a new list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may not go out on שבת with a needle with an eye, a ring with a seal, a כוליאר, a כובלת, or a flask of balsam oil.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and the Sages disagree about liability
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a woman who went out with any of these items is חייב חטאת. חכמים exempt her for the כובלת and the balsam flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she did go out with these items, she must bring a קרבן חטאת. This is the view of רבי מאיר. חכמים say she is exempt if it was a כובלת or a flask of balsam oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now tells us what happens if a woman did go out with one of these items. רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree about two of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says all five items count as carrying a load, which is a Torah violation, so she must bring a חטאת. חכמים agree about the first three. But they see the כובלת and the balsam flask as ornaments a woman wears, so wearing them is not Torah-level carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: She must bring a קרבן חטאת, the offering for breaking a Torah prohibition by mistake
They exempt her, meaning she does not owe a חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: פוטרין (exempt) does not mean she may go out with these items. The משנה already said she may not go out with them. חכמים only mean she does not owe a חטאת for it.
steps.whatToRemember: All five items are forbidden. The dispute is only about the two ornaments, the כובלת and the balsam flask. רבי מאיר says she owes a חטאת. חכמים say she does not.

phrases.english: And if she did go out
she is liable to bring a sin-offering
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages exempt her
for a kovelet and for a flask of balsam oil.
phrases.notes: חכמים see these two as ornaments, not loads.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם יָצְתָה חַיֶּיבֶת חַטָּאת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the same משנה. After the list of forbidden items, it tells us what she owes if she went out with them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: she is חייב חטאת for any of the five items. חכמים: she is exempt for the כובלת and the balsam flask, since these are ornaments.

steps.title: עולא: the reverse applies to a man
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the משנה's ring rules are reversed for a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: עולא said: For a man, it is the reverse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens on the משנה. עולא says the ring rule for women is flipped for men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a woman, a sealed ring is not jewelry. So going out with it is carrying, and she is חייב. A plain ring is jewelry for her, so it is fine. עולא says it is the reverse for a man: a sealed ring is fine for him, and a plain ring counts as carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
And the reverse of them
A ring with a seal (from the משנה)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Ulla said:
And the reverse of these applies to a man.
phrases.notes: A sealed ring is fine for a man. A plain ring is a burden for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה listed in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a man the ring rules are reversed: a sealed ring is permitted and a plain ring is forbidden.

steps.title: The גמרא draws out עולא's underlying principle
steps.stepSummary: From עולא's words, the גמרא infers a general rule: men's items are never fit for women, and women's items are never fit for men.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems עולא holds: anything fit for a man is not fit for a woman, and anything fit for a woman is not fit for a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the thinking behind עולא's statement. It is also setting up a principle that will now be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלמא ('so it seems') signals that the גמרא is drawing a conclusion. Something counts as jewelry only for the gender that normally wears it. This sharp line is the target of the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems / apparently (introduces a conclusion)
He holds
An item that is fit / suitable

phrases.english: Apparently Ulla holds:
any item that is fit for a man
is not fit for a woman,
and an item that is fit for a woman
is not fit for a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general principle out of עולא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items count as clothing or jewelry only for the gender that normally wears them.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects from shepherds wearing sacks
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא: anyone may go out in sacks, even though only shepherds normally wear them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Shepherds may go out in sacks. This was not said only about shepherds but about everyone. It mentions shepherds only because they usually go out in sacks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the principle from step 10. A ברייתא shows that something one group normally wears is allowed for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sacks are normal clothing only for shepherds, yet anyone may wear them on שבת. So something counts as clothing even for people who do not usually wear it. By the same logic, a man's sealed ring should count as jewelry for a woman, which goes against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shepherds
Sacks (rough garments)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
Shepherds may go out in sacks.
And they did not say this about shepherds alone,
but about any person.
Only, it is the usual way of shepherds
to go out in sacks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle drawn in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that a man's item cannot be fit for a woman, and the reverse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one group's normal garment counts as clothing for everyone, then one gender's jewelry should also count as jewelry for the other gender.

steps.title: רב יוסף: women are a people unto themselves
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains עולא differently. Men and women are like two separate peoples, so the shepherd case does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: עולא holds that women are a separate people.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers his own challenge by explaining עולא's reasoning in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shepherds and other men are all one group. So what shepherds wear counts as clothing for every man. But men and women are like two separate peoples, so what is normal for one does not count for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier approach)
Women are a people unto themselves

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a statement about women in general. It only means that, for what counts as clothing or jewelry on שבת, men's and women's norms are judged separately.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Ulla holds
women are a people unto themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the shepherd challenge by drawing a line between gender and profession.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק): difference in profession versus difference in gender.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Men and women are like different professions, so the shepherd case would apply to them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Men and women are like two separate peoples. Their norms do not carry over the way they do among men of different jobs.

steps.title: אביי objects from a woman carrying found תפילין
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: both a man and a woman may wear found תפילין to bring them in on שבת. But women are exempt from תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Someone who finds תפילין brings them in one pair at a time, whether a man or a woman. If women are a separate people, this is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and women are exempt from every such מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's explanation. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who finds תפילין in a field on שבת may wear them and bring them in, because worn תפילין count as clothing, not carrying. Women are exempt from תפילין, so for them תפילין are 'men's items.' Yet the ברייתא lets a woman wear them too, which suggests a man's item can count as clothing for a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Pair by pair (one head and one arm תפילין at a time)
A positive מצוה bound by time
Exempt (feminine plural)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that women are exempt from מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא is central. Here it is used to show that תפילין are a 'man's item,' setting up a strong challenge.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
One who finds tefillin
brings them in one pair at a time,
both a man and a woman.
And if you say
women are a people unto themselves,
but it is a positive מצוה
that is bound by time,
and from every positive מצוה bound by time
women are exempt?
phrases.notes: So why may a woman wear them to bring them in?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that women are a separate people, so men's items are not clothing for them.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין are a man's item, since women are exempt. Yet a woman may wear them as clothing to save them on שבת. So a man's item can count as clothing for a woman.

steps.title: רבי מאיר holds women are obligated in תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about found תפילין follows רבי מאיר. He holds תפילין are worn even at night and on שבת, so the מצוה is not time-bound and women are obligated in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, רבי מאיר holds that night is a time for תפילין, and שבת is a time for תפילין. So it is a מצות עשה שלא הזמן גרמא, and in every מצות עשה שלא הזמן גרמא, women are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's question from step 13. The ברייתא lets women wear found תפילין because, according to רבי מאיר, women are actually obligated in תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had argued that תפילין are a 'men's item', yet women may wear them, which would contradict עולא's rule. The answer is that according to רבי מאיר תפילין apply at all times, including night and שבת. That makes it a מצות עשה שלא הזמן גרמא, which women are obligated in, so תפילין are not purely a men's item for him.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)
Night is a valid time for wearing tefillin
A positive מצוה that is not tied to a specific time
Women are obligated

steps.confusionAlert: The usual rule is that women are exempt from תפילין, because we hold שבת and night are NOT times for תפילין. This answer only works because רבי מאיר holds the opposite.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer protects עולא's rule that men's items are not for women. The ברייתא turns out to be no exception at all, since for רבי מאיר תפילין belong to women too.

phrases.english: There, Rabbi Meir holds:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא about found תפילין.

phrases.english: night is a time for tefillin,
and Shabbat is a time for tefillin.
So it is a positive מצוה
that is not caused by time,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא —
phrases.english: and every positive מצוה not caused by time —
women are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the ברייתא to רבי מאיר's specific view, which removes the contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תפילין are a men-only item, yet women may wear them, so עולא's rule seems broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר women are obligated in תפילין, so wearing them is natural for women too. רב יוסף's explanation of עולא (women are a people unto themselves) stands.

steps.title: Isn't wearing a ring an unusual way of carrying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. It asks how a woman wearing a sealed ring can be liable, since carrying an object on one's finger is not the normal way to carry.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it carrying out in a backhanded (unusual) way?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, where רבי מאיר makes a woman liable for going out with a sealed ring. It challenges this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sealed ring is not jewelry for a woman, so it counts as an ordinary object being carried. People normally carry objects in the hand, not on a finger. Carrying in an unusual way (כלאחר יד) is not a Torah violation, so why should she be liable?

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out from one domain to another
In a backhanded, unusual way, which is not a Torah-level violation

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether she carried at all. It is whether this way of carrying is normal enough to make her liable on a Torah level.

phrases.english: But isn't it carrying out
phrases.notes: Refers to the woman in the משנה who goes out with a sealed ring.

phrases.english: in a backhanded (unusual) way!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תפילין side-discussion and returns to the משנה's ring ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה that a woman wearing a sealed ring is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ring is not jewelry, wearing it on a finger is an unusual way of carrying, and that should not bring liability.

steps.title: The woman is a charity treasurer
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the משנה is talking about a woman who works as a charity treasurer. For her, wearing a sealed ring is normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: We are dealing with a woman who is a treasurer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question by narrowing the case. The woman in the משנה is a treasurer who normally wears a sealed ring for her job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A treasurer uses a seal to stamp things, so wearing a sealed ring is her normal way of carrying it. Wearing it is therefore not unusual carrying for her, and she can be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A female treasurer, for example of charity funds
We are dealing with (this case)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
We are dealing with a woman who is a treasurer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כלאחר יד question in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a special situation (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A woman never normally wears a sealed ring, so wearing it is unusual carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a treasurer, wearing a sealed ring is normal, so it counts as real carrying.

steps.title: That answer doesn't work for the man
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points out that the treasurer answer explains the woman. It does not explain why a man would be liable for wearing an unsealed ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: You answered for a woman. What is there to say about a man?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges רבי ירמיה's answer. It does not cover the reversed case that עולא taught for men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said the rules flip for a man: he is liable for an unsealed ring. An unsealed ring is jewelry, which is a women's item, so wearing it would be unusual carrying for him too. The treasurer idea cannot explain that case.

keyTerms.meaning: You have answered (resolved)
What is there to say?

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
You have answered for a woman;
for a man, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: Refers to עולא's reversed case: a man with an unsealed ring.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּרַצְתָּ אִשָּׁה, אִישׁ מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's answer in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer only fits the woman's case. The man's liability for an unsealed ring (from עולא) is still unexplained.

steps.title: People really do carry rings on the finger when delivering them
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a wife carrying her husband's sealed ring to a box, or a husband carrying his wife's unsealed ring to a craftsman, normally puts it on the finger. So this is a normal way of carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Sometimes a man gives his wife a sealed ring to take to the box, and she puts it on her hand until she reaches the box. And sometimes a woman gives her husband an unsealed ring to take to a craftsman to repair, and he puts it on his hand until he reaches the craftsman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רבי ירמיה's answer and gives a new one that works for both the woman and the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone carries another person's ring on an errand, he or she often slips it onto a finger so it won't get lost. That is a normal, common way of carrying a ring, so it is not כלאחר יד. This explains the woman's sealed ring and the man's unsealed ring together.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier answer)
A seal (engraved signet)
A box, used for safekeeping
A craftsman

steps.whatToRemember: The woman (sealed ring) and the man (unsealed ring) are liable because carrying a ring on the finger while delivering it is a normal way of carrying, not כלאחר יד.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's answer covers both the משנה and עולא's reversed case with one idea. That is why it replaces רבי ירמיה's narrow treasurer answer.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Sometimes a man gives his wife
a ring that has a seal on it
to take it to the box,
and she puts it on her hand (finger)
until she reaches the box.
And sometimes a woman gives her husband
a ring that has no seal on it
to take it to a craftsman to repair,
and he puts it on his hand (finger)
until he reaches the craftsman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי ירמיה's answer after רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new general reason (normal manner of carrying) that covers both cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wearing a ring that isn't one's own type of jewelry is always unusual carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wearing a ring on the finger while delivering it is a normal way to carry, so both the woman and the man are liable.

steps.title: What is a כוליאר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about the כוליאר and the כובלת, and asks what a כוליאר is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a woman may not go out with a כוליאר or with a כובלת. What is a כוליאר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next words of the משנה and asks what an unfamiliar object is. This sets up the definitions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before we can understand the law, we need to know what the object is. The משנה uses rare words, so the גמרא first clarifies the meaning of כוליאר.

keyTerms.meaning: An item a woman wears, defined in the next step
Another item a woman wears, defined in the next step
What is? (a request for a definition)

phrases.english: Nor with a kulyar, nor with a kovelet.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: What is a kulyar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ring discussion and moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word כוליאר (and, by extension, כובלת)

steps.title: A brooch, and a bundle of fragrant herbs
steps.stepSummary: רב defines a כוליאר as a brooch and a כובלת as a bundle of fragrant herbs. רב אסי agrees about the כובלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said a כוליאר is a brooch. For כובלת, רב said it is a bundle of fragrant herbs. רב אסי also said it is a bundle of fragrant herbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by defining both words from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוליאר is a pin that fastens a garment's collar. A כובלת is a small bundle of sweet-smelling herbs. Because רב אסי gives the same definition, the meaning of כובלת is well supported.

keyTerms.meaning: A brooch or pin for fastening a garment
A bundle of fragrant herbs (a perfume pouch)
And so too said (another אמורא who agrees)

phrases.english: Rav said: A brooch.
Kovelet: Rav said:
A bundle of fragrant herbs.
And similarly Rav Asi said:
A bundle of fragrant herbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כוליאר = a brooch. כובלת = a bundle of fragrant herbs (רב, and רב אסי agrees).

steps.title: Three opinions on going out with a herb bundle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records three views. רבי מאיר says she is חייב חטאת. חכמים say it is forbidden but she is פטור. רבי אליעזר says it is allowed even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A woman may not go out with a herb bundle, and if she did, she must bring a חטאת. This is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say she may not go out with it, but if she did, she is פטור. רבי אליעזר says a woman may go out with a herb bundle even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing a three-way argument about the כובלת that was just defined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels here. Forbidden by the Torah (חייב חטאת), forbidden only by the Rabbis (פטור, but don't do it), and fully allowed (לכתחילה). Our משנה, which says 'she may not go out,' fits at least רבי מאיר or חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Must bring a sin-offering, meaning she broke a Torah law by mistake
Exempt from a קרבן, though still forbidden by the Rabbis
From the start, fully allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Here פטורה does not mean 'allowed.' It means no Torah violation, but the Rabbis still say not to do it. Only רבי אליעזר's 'לכתחילה' means truly permitted.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
She may not go out with a herb bundle,
and if she went out, she is liable to a sin-offering,
the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: She may not go out,
but if she went out, she is exempt.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A woman may go out with a herb bundle even from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the law about the item that was just defined
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: חייב חטאת. חכמים: forbidden, but פטור. רבי אליעזר: allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: What is the basis of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the three views disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do they disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the three opinions. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A three-way split like this needs a reason. The גמרא wants to know what each תנא thinks the herb bundle is, and why that leads to his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רבי מאיר, חכמים, and רבי אליעזר

steps.title: Burden versus ornament
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds the herb bundle is a משאוי (burden). חכמים hold it is a תכשיט (ornament), but they forbid it in case she takes it off to show others and then carries it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds it is a burden. The Rabbis hold it is an ornament, but she might take it off and show it to others, and come to carry it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the views of רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is a משאוי, carrying it out is a real Torah מלאכה, so רבי מאיר says she is חייב חטאת. If it is a תכשיט, wearing it is not carrying, so she is פטור. Still, חכמים made a גזירה because she may remove it to show it off and then carry it in the street.

keyTerms.meaning: A burden, a thing that is carried and not worn
An ornament, which counts as part of one's clothing
She takes it off and shows it to others
To carry it

steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between משאוי and תכשיט is the key idea of this whole פרק. It decides whether wearing something counts as carrying.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds it is a burden.
And the Rabbis hold it is an ornament,
but perhaps she will remove it and show it,
and come to carry it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about the basis of the argument
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר: it is a משאוי, so carrying it is a Torah violation. חכמים: it is a תכשיט, but it is forbidden because of a rabbinic concern that she will take it off and carry it.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר is not worried
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that only a woman with a bad odor wears herbs. She will not take them off to show anyone, so there is no fear she will carry them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: Who usually wears this? A woman with a bad odor. A woman with a bad odor will not take it off and show it, so she will not come to carry it four אמות in רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's view that the herb bundle is allowed even from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר agrees that it is a תכשיט, but he rejects the גזירה of חכמים. A woman who wears herbs to cover a bad smell would not want to remove them, because then people would notice her smell. So the worry about carrying does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose way is it to put it on?
A woman whose body odor is bad
Four cubits in the public domain, the distance that makes carrying a Torah violation

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer holds:
Whose practice is it to put it on?
A woman whose odor is bad.

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה שֶׁרֵיחָהּ רָע לָא שָׁלְפָא וּמַחְוְיָא,
phrases.english: A woman whose odor is bad does not remove it and show it,
and will not come to carry it
four cubits in the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: מַאן דִּרְכַּהּ לְמִירְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer by explaining the third opinion
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר: it is a תכשיט, and the גזירה does not apply, because a woman with a bad odor will never remove it to show it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says משאוי, so she is חייב. חכמים say תכשיט with a גזירה, so she is פטור but it is forbidden. רבי אליעזר says תכשיט with no גזירה, so it is allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: Another source says רבי אליעזר only exempts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's position. Another ברייתא says he is פוטר for a כובלת and a balsam flask, which suggests it is still forbidden from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי אליעזר exempts a woman who goes out with a herb bundle or with a flask of balsam oil!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between two ברייתות about what רבי אליעזר holds. The answer will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, רבי אליעזר allows the כובלת לכתחילה. In this ברייתא he only says פוטר, and in the laws of שבת that usually means 'exempt, but forbidden.' So which is his real view?

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, meaning no קרבן, but usually still forbidden לכתחילה
A small flask of balsam oil (perfume)

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
Rabbi Eliezer exempts
with a herb bundle and with a flask of balsam oil!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of רבי אליעזר that was just explained
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's statement that רבי אליעזר allows a כובלת לכתחילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא has רבי אליעזר saying only פוטר. In the laws of שבת, פוטר implies it is still forbidden לכתחילה, which contradicts his full permission.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר was answering two different opponents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The word פטור was רבי אליעזר's reply to רבי מאיר, who said חייב חטאת. The word מותר לכתחילה was his reply to the חכמים, who said פטור אבל אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a problem. One statement was made when רבי אליעזר was arguing with רבי מאיר. The other was made when he was arguing with the חכמים. When he was arguing with רבי מאיר, who said she is חייב חטאת, רבי אליעזר said: 'פטור.' When he was arguing with the חכמים, who said פטור but forbidden, רבי אליעזר said: 'It is מותר even לכתחילה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 25. It explains that רבי אליעזר's two statements do not clash, because each one was a reply to a different opponent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second ברייתא, רבי אליעזר only had to push back against רבי מאיר's claim that she must bring a קרבן. So he just said פטור, which was enough to win that point. Against the חכמים, who already agreed she is פטור, the real argument was about לכתחילה, so there he said it is fully מותר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is the formula for answering a contradiction.
When he was standing against, meaning when he was responding to a specific opponent
Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden to do
Permitted even from the start
A sin-offering, brought for accidentally breaking a serious prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's true view is מותר לכתחילה. The word פטור in the other ברייתא was only his answer to רבי מאיר's claim of חיוב חטאת. It was not his full position.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read פטור here as meaning 'פטור אבל אסור.' רבי אליעזר said פטור only because he was rejecting רבי מאיר's חייב. It does not mean he holds the act is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. A תנא's words can be shaped by the opponent he is answering. So a short word like פטור may not be his full opinion.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
phrases.notes: The standard opening of an answer to a contradiction.

phrases.english: This statement was when he was responding to Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says פוטר.

phrases.english: That statement was when he was responding to the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says מותר לכתחילה.

phrases.english: When he was responding to Rabbi Meir
who said she is liable to bring a sin-offering,
he (Rabbi Eliezer) said: exempt.
phrases.notes: Saying פטור was enough to reject רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: When he was responding to the Rabbis
who said she is exempt but it is forbidden,
he said: it is permitted even from the start.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר's real, full position.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא כִּי קָאֵי — אַדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of Step 25 by putting the two ברייתות in their context.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual split: each statement is a reply to a different opponent (אוקימתא of the dialogue context).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word פוטר in the second ברייתא seemed to show that רבי אליעזר holds the act is forbidden לכתחילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: פוטר was only a reply to רבי מאיר's חייב חטאת. Against the חכמים, רבי אליעזר clearly says מותר לכתחילה, and that is his true view.
